classification.difficultyReason: Identify quadrilaterals from their markings and apply their directly taught angle properties.

content.prompt: Find the missing angles. You will need to use properties of quadrilaterals.

spec.description: Wide rectangle with four right-angle markers, two upper 90° givens and empty boxes inside the lower corners.
spec.mathematics: All four marked interior angles are right angles. Retain both redundant upper-angle labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Both lower response boxes remain empty in the question diagram.

answer.worked: Both lower angles are right angles, as shown by their square markers. Each is $90^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Sloping parallelogram with two distinct parallel-marker families, four interior angle arcs, upper-right 34° and lower-right 146° givens.
spec.mathematics: Opposite sides are parallel. Opposite angles are equal. The lower-left angle corresponds to 34° and the upper-left angle to 146°.
spec.answerVisibility: Lower-left and upper-left answer boxes remain empty. White box interiors are structural masks that preserve the source scaffold.

answer.worked: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. The lower-left angle is $34^{\circ}$ and the upper-left angle is $146^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Horizontal kite with single ticks on its left-side pair, double ticks on its right-side pair, four angle arcs and an empty upper-angle box.
spec.mathematics: The left and right angles are 70° and 40°. The lower angle is 125°. The equal opposite angles lie between the unequal side pairs.
spec.answerVisibility: The upper-angle box remains empty. All three supplied angles remain visible.

answer.worked: The top and bottom angles lie between the unequal side pairs of the kite, so they are equal. The missing angle is $125^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Horizontal rhombus with one equality tick on every side, four angle arcs, left 50° and lower 130° givens, and empty upper and right response boxes.
spec.mathematics: All four sides are equal. Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: The upper and right answer boxes remain empty; both supplied angles remain visible.

answer.worked: Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal. The upper angle is $130^{\circ}$ and the right angle is $50^{\circ}$.
